annotations.title: Save an edit to your draft

description: Requires a TechFabric engineer's Microsoft sign-in (scope blog.write). Save a new version of your draft (state drafted): the whole Markdown, and base_hash, the hash of the version you edited (draft.base_hash from get_status, or your last update_draft's text_hash). Answers in a second or two; the preview rebuilds in the background. It runs no checks: lint_draft the edit first, then check_draft with the id. Refused if the draft changed since base_hash or is open in the browser editor. The engineer may also edit and save it in the draft app: start each edit from a fresh get_status. Never publishes.

app_instance.description: The draft app only, never an agent: the view whose own unsaved edits this save is

base_hash.description: The hash of the version your edit started from: draft.base_hash from the get_status you edited from, or the text_hash your last update_draft returned. It stays good after that save is committed

base_sha.description: Instead of base_hash: draft.base_sha from get_status, the commit your edit started from

client_confirmed.description: Only when the engineer tells you they have the client's confirmation to name the client this draft names (its client:, or a client in its text the register doesn't approve). Recorded under the engineer's name with the draft and its text; never send it on your own judgement. It covers naming the client, not results: numbers still need sources.

first_hand.description: First-hand claims only the engineer can source, which the fact-check flagged first_hand (first_hand_to_confirm): each the sentence exactly as quoted, with what it rests on. Sending it asks the engineer; it never confirms anything on your word. check_draft asks them in their client (an elicitation) where it can, otherwise answers with a question and a one-time confirmation: ask them that question, and only if they say yes, send it back as first_hand_confirmation with the same first_hand. submit_draft and update_draft answer with the question and confirmation too, which come back on check_draft with the id. Never a client's result: a number about a client needs the client's confirmation, as a source.

basis.description: measured: we measured or ran it; our_product: how our own product works; client_told_us: what a client said (not their numbers); customers_ask: what our customers ask; we_did_it: what we built, saw or decided; own_work: first-hand, from the engineer's own work

claim.description: The sentence, exactly as the fact-check quoted it

kind.description: Optional: the draft's kind, which is fixed when it is submitted. Sent, it must match (get_status says it).

markdown.description: The whole post, with its frontmatter

sources.description: New sources, replacing the ones sent before: the engineer's own words, which the fact-check reads a post's claims against, or a case study's numbers are checked against.

name: update_draft

first_hand.description: When first_hand was sent: nothing is recorded here. The engineer is asked on check_draft with the id (in their client, where it can ask them), or, for update_draft in a client that can't, this carries the question and a one-time confirmation to hand back on check_draft only after they say yes

next_action.description: The one next step. Do what instruction says; call is the tool and the arguments the server already knows

steps.description: Where the draft is, step by step (the same steps the progress notifications name): done, active (under way now), pending or failed

text_hash.description: The saved text's sha256: the next update_draft's base_hash

title: Save an edit to your draft
